tool_args.rationale: The history gap and transient lag favor a coupled memory state. The pilot already spans the target horizon, but every memory state must be reconstructed from its irregular prefix. Additional fine trajectories are the targeted way to constrain the memory timescale and coupling before fresh confirmation.

considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: Cheaper, but the main uncertainty is parameter identification within the coupled-memory model, not which mechanism to test first.
Five endpoint targets with the same prefix time grid and similar forecast horizons provide little leverage to separate the memory timescale from the coupling strength.

considered_alternatives.option: single-mode Maxwell decay or Kelvin–Voigt creep
considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: Maxwell decay predicts opposite signs for upward and downward input steps, but all five targets are positive. Kelvin–Voigt creep omits the observed dependence on history at matched endpoints.
